subject: CareVista: header obfuscation feasibility & next steps
messages:
From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Fraser <sarah.fraser@carevista.com>, Mike Chen <mike.chen@carevista.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>, procurement@carevista.com
Date: Tue, 12 May 2026 16:02:00 -0700
Subject: CareVista: header obfuscation feasibility & next steps

Hi Sarah / Mike —

Thanks again for the call today. Summary of the requirements we captured on our side and proposed next steps below so we can align engineering + procurement: 

Key points we heard
- CareVista will retain request/response logs for troubleshooting but needs sensitive headers removed or obfuscated before storage (Authorization, Cookie, X-Trace-Id / Trace-Token, and any custom PII headers).
- Data residency: logs must remain in US regions only.
- Retention target: 30 days by default; procurement may request a 90-day pilot for a short-term trial, but default programmatically enforced retention is preferred.
- You also need an evidence package (design doc + sample scrubbed logs) for your internal risk/compliance review and for procurement.

Options we can deliver (high-level) — pros/cons included in attached PDF: redwood-logging-options-20260512.pdf
A) Edge scrubbing (recommended): strip listed headers at our edge before logs enter the ingest pipeline. Lowest storage risk; impacts runtime debugging unless we offer temporary debug traces.
B) Non-reversible hashing of trace IDs (per-customer salt): preserves the ability to correlate events while preventing RAW trace IDs from being stored. Salt rotation schedule is configurable; hashed IDs are not reversible without the salt.
C) Pseudonymization service / encrypted logs: store encrypted headers in a KMS-protected blob for emergency incident retrieval under strict audit + approval. Higher complexity and cost.

Engineering notes / constraints
- If you require trace ID reversibility for incident response, we recommend option C with a gated decrypt workflow (audit + approved request). Reversibility is not compatible with option B unless the salt is stored and accessible (reduces compliance benefits).
- We can scope a POC that produces a small set of scrubbed logs (sanitized sample) within 48 hours once we have the header list you want removed vs hashed.

Proposed immediate next steps
1) Please confirm the final header list (Authorization, Cookie, X-Trace-Id, X-Session-User, X-Client-Email are common candidates). 2) Procurement: which template/terms should Sean reference? 3) We will deliver a sanitized sample and the attached design doc by 2026-05-14 pending confirmation of the header list.

I attached: redwood-logging-options-20260512.pdf (design + tradeoffs).

Would you like a separate call with Jordan (our infra lead) to walk the scrub flow and hashing tradeoffs? I can propose two slots tomorrow (Wed) or Thursday.

Thanks,
Mina Haddad

From: Sarah Fraser <sarah.fraser@carevista.com>

Cc: Mike Chen <mike.chen@carevista.com>, procurement@carevista.com
Date: Wed, 13 May 2026 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Re: CareVista: header obfuscation feasibility & next steps

Thanks Mina — helpful summary. Couple follow-ups from security and procurement: 

1) Hashing reversibility: we need to be explicit. For incident response we generally need to be able to map a trace back to internal IDs (for edge correlators). If you propose non-reversible hashing, can you confirm whether you support a reversible HMAC workflow (HMAC with customer-managed key) or only irreversible hashes?

2) KMS / key separation: our security team requires that any salts/keys used to pseudonymize customer-specific identifiers be stored in a customer-isolated KMS (or at least with strict access controls). Does Redwood support per-customer KMS integration (Bring Your Own Key)?

3) Evidence: procurement needs a short packet that says how headers are removed and where the scrubbed logs live (S3 bucket name / region + access controls). Mike will upload our security questionnaire (attached, carevista-security-questionnaire.pdf) — please fill the sections related to logging and retention.

Also — could you provide a small sample of scrubbed logs from the demo (even synthetic data) so our security team can validate that PII is removed? That would speed review.

Thanks,
Sarah Fraser
Head of Security
CareVista Health

Looping in a procurement/terms note for the thread. Quick recommendations: 

- Offer two commercial tracks on the pilot: (1) standard: 30-day retention + edge scrubbing (no reversible trace IDs), included in hosted pricing; (2) pilot extended-retention: 90 days with gated decrypted retrieval (audit trail + chargeable admin request) as an add-on at a defined monthly fee. This keeps our default compliance posture simple while giving CareVista the option to pay for extended debugability.

- For KMS: we should confirm BYOK support for keys used in reversible workflows. If BYOK is required, include the Private deployment option as the long-term path (we can do BYOK in Redwood Private; hosted can support customer-managed keys with limitations).

- I recommend we deliver the synthetic scrubbed sample to Sarah ASAP, then present a single-page tradeoff doc for procurement that maps to the two commercial tracks above. Jordan: can you confirm if the sample requires any infra changes or can be produced from our staging pipeline?
